Model: Noise. Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types/13 Noise

Wave morphs particle noise through white noise to metallic noise. Timbre changes noise sample-rate reduction and the pitch of the metallic component; Shape blends the noise with a pitched waveform. The saved cycling-envelope routes sweep both noise character controls, while keyboard tracking counteracts part of the Timbre movement. Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types/13 Noise
Low-pass filter. Saved cutoff: 0.174; resonance: 0.415. Microfreak/UG/07 Filter/01 Modifying Sound/01 Low Pass Filter
Main envelope: attack 0.000, decay/release 0.510, sustain 0.430. Amp Mod is on, so the main envelope controls loudness. Microfreak/UG/09 Envelope Gen/03 Envelope Stages
Cycling Envelope mode: Loop. Stored RiseLvl 0.233, RiseSlp 1.000, FallLvl 0.222, FallSlp 1.000, Hold 0.217, Amount 0.236. Microfreak/UG/09 Envelope Gen/06 Cycling Envelope
Sample-and-Hold, clock sync off; stored normalized rate: 0.999. Microfreak/UG/08 LFO/01 LFO Shape · Microfreak/UG/08 LFO/02 LFO Rate
Amounts use the signed normalized range −1…+1. Microfreak/UG/05 Connections/02 Matrix and Encoder/01 Sources and Destinations
All other saved matrix amounts are zero.

Hold several notes in paraphonic mode to hear the noise-and-pitched blend across the keyboard. The looping Cycling Envelope sweeps noise character while key position changes Timbre and cutoff. The LFO modulates its own rate and the Cycling Envelope’s amount and fall, so the saved modulation wiring can produce changing motion without manual knob turns. Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types/13 Noise · Microfreak/UG/05 Connections/02 Matrix and Encoder/01 Sources and Destinations

NoiseBusters opens GitP/A/Session/26/10/26-Mon; the unedited commentary recording starts with codekiln saying “119 NoiseBusters.” The first 01:49 has no controller changes, so the opening plays the saved sound; cutoff, cycling-envelope and oscillator changes follow from 01:49. The saved factory baseline does not capture those unsaved changes.

With V.Analog, the panel's Wave knob sets Detune between the two waves, Timbre sets Shape, a variable square from narrow pulse through full square to hard-sync formants, and Shape sets Wave, a variable saw from triangle to sawtooth. Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types/06 VAnalog

Play single notes low on the keyboard. Each note starts a short main-envelope pluck that opens the low-pass filter and, through the negative ENV → Wave route, pulls the waveform and timbre on the attack. The looping Cycling Envelope at high amount adds a repeating pulse, and the small glide joins legato notes. Pressure brightens the timbre. Microfreak/UG/05 Connections/02 Matrix and Encoder/01 Sources and Destinations · Microfreak/UG/09 Envelope Gen/06 Cycling Envelope

Hold a note while the cycling envelope moves speech formants and the filtered random LFO changes Word and pulls the low-pass cutoff downward. These saved routes couple changing syllables with changing brightness. Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types/11 Speech

Expression raises filter resonance and the Arp/Seq Rate assignment. The rate route affects note repetition when the arpeggiator or sequencer is running; its presence alone does not establish that either was active in a performance. Hold a note and let the slow main-envelope attack bring the noise in. With Shape saved at zero, the Noise model starts from noise alone; Wave selects the noise character and Timbre applies sample-rate reduction. Microfreak/UG/06 Dig Osc/03 Types/13 Noise

The Cycling Envelope moves noise Wave, Timbre and band-pass cutoff together. The slow filtered random LFO varies the envelope Rise and Fall settings, so the saved modulation changes the pace of those sweeps. The matrix has no nonzero pressure or keyboard modulation routes. Microfreak/UG/09 Envelope Gen/06 Cycling Envelope
